summary.text: 国 means “country” or “nation.” It is the simplified form of 國, whose enclosure 囗 marks territory and whose inner 或 supplies a sound cue. The 玉 inside 国 is a graphic replacement for 或, not the historical sound element.

formation.text: The source graph 國 is phonosemantic: 囗 contributes the territory meaning, while 或 supplies a sound cue. The curated Western Zhou bronze-style image shows this enclosed arrangement as a modern redraw. In 国, 玉 replaces 或; why 玉 was chosen is not explained.

components.text: In 國, 囗 marks a boundary or territory. Some Warring States forms are reported with 匚 or 𠃊 in the same boundary-marker role. This component belongs to 國, the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
In 國, 或 is the phonetic element; its original depicted referent is not established. It is replaced by 玉 in 国, so it is not a component of the current graph.

sound_limitation.text: The cited reconstructions show a sound relationship but do not identify 或’s original depicted referent. Modern readings alone do not prove its role in 國.

sound.text: Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstructions, 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ, are similar but differ in their initial consonant. These are reconstructions, not direct records of ancient speech.

components.text: 玉 is the visible inner element in 国, in the position occupied by 或 in 國. It is a graphic replacement; why 玉 was chosen is not established.

history.text: The curated image is a modern redraw of a Western Zhou bronze-script-style form: an angular inner element sits inside an enclosure. It illustrates the reported structure of 國, not an artifact or a proven sequence of graphic stages.

國 with 囗 is reported in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions for “country/state.” Warring States forms may vary the boundary marker; later bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts also use 國 with this meaning. These examples attest usage but do not establish a sequence of graphic stages or later meanings.

A Han-dynasty dictionary account analyzes 國 as 囗 plus 或 and glosses it as 邦. The proposed reading of 或 as “country” in the He zun inscription is disputed; another interpretation takes it as 域, “territory.”

国 is reported as simplified from 國, with 或 replaced by 玉, and as the Japanese shinjitai corresponding to 國. The exact pathway and date of this graphic change are not established by the cited evidence.

uncertainties.text: The secure earliest attestation of the spoken word meaning “country/state” remains unsettled: the proposed He zun reading of 或 as 國 is disputed, and the cited research does not include a complete inscription survey.
A dated semantic path from boundary or territory to polity, and the chronology of later senses such as “nation-state,” are not established.
The evidence reports the graphic replacement 或 → 玉 but does not establish its precise historical pathway or why 玉 was selected.

senses.period: Western Zhou inscriptions reported; exact earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions are reported to use 國 for “country/state.” This supports the sense in that period, while the disputed He zun reading of 或 leaves the word’s earliest attestation unsettled.
The character is currently used for “nation” and “country.” The evidence does not date how this range developed from the older country/state sense.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a dated semantic transition from territory or state to the current range “nation, country, nation-state.”

overview.text: 国 means “country” or “nation.” It comes from 國, where 或 sits inside a boundary marker. In 国, 玉 occupies that inner position; in 國, 或 supplies the sound cue.

components.text: In 國, 囗 marks a boundary or territory. It belongs to the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
In 國, 或 is the sound element, though its original pictured referent is unsettled. 国 has 玉 in its place.
玉 is the visible inner form in 国, replacing 或 from 國; the reason for this choice is not established.

takeaway.text: The sound element in 國 is 或; 玉 in 国 is a later graphic replacement.

relationships.text: 囗 marks the boundary or territory in 國, the traditional graph from which 国 is simplified.
或 is analyzed as the sound component of 國, from which 国 is simplified; the sound comparison uses Old Chinese reconstructions.
玉 occupies the inner position in 国 where 或 appears in 國; it is the reported graphic replacement in the simplified form.
国 is reported as simplified from 國, with 玉 replacing 或 in the inner position.
